body: Two things jump out. First, FR-010 builds a headline metric — the 'Unexplained Variance Gap' — on a number that isn't established anywhere in this spec. It asserts a 'literature-derived maximum (0.60)' for R² and cites Oke (1982), but Oke's paper is about the surface energy balance of heat islands; it contains no regression R² ceiling for OSM-derived covariates predicting Landsat LST. The whole gap metric is only as good as that 0.60, and right now it's a number wearing a citation as a costume. If observed R² comes out at, say, 0.55, the spec would report a tiny 'gap' and invite the conclusion that OSM features capture nearly everything — when the actual ceiling is unknown and city- and covariate-dependent. Either derive a defensible upper bound (e.g., from the noise floor of the LST composite itself, or from comparable published OSM/LST regressions) or drop the metric. Second, the memory fallback block is duplicated verbatim (the trigger/action/failure/logging/integrity bullets appear twice in a row), and there's an internal contradiction: FR-005's integrity clause says 'The pipeline must not crash; it must complete with the degraded model set,' while the fallback says exceeding 6 GB aborts with error code 99 — the pipeline both must not crash and must crash. Also worth a look: FR-008 applies permutation-based FDR, but with strong spatial autocorrelation (which the spec itself measures via Moran's I), naive row-permutation of spatial data will understate p-values; the permutation scheme needs to respect spatial structure (e.g., block permutations) or the 'correction' can make things worse.
